Cape Town Fire UCT Historic archive burns

By: Liz Fish | Delivery

Proposal


Show:

Unique Selling Point:
The fire that ripped through UCT late Sunday afternoon is absolutely devastating for African history, it is one of the great historic losses of this century! Academics and archivists posted what they were working on and the full extent of what was lost will be uncovered in the next few days.

Summary:
An unattended vagrant fire spread rapidly through old stone pines on the slopes of Table Mountain and devastated the Rhodes Memorial Restaurant, then the historic Mosterts Mill which dates back to the 17th Century and various historic buildings in the area. Students were evacuated from their residences. Then sweeping across UCT the Science and Botany buildings were hit, fortunately they managed to move the explosive chemicals in time but it destroyed The Bolus Herbarium with plant species dating back to the 1800 many of which are now extinct. Then the heart of UCT , the Jagger Reading room went up in flames and the African Studies collection was destroyed.

Late Sunday evening two arsonists were arrested for starting small fires above Woodstock which were driven by strong winds across towards Cape Town and Vredehoek was evacuated last night. The fire is still raging driven my strong winds and homes above Woodstock are being evacuated as firefighters battle the blaze


Further information:
But the biggest loss remains that of the UCT African Studies collection and the rare plant collection in the Bolus Herbarium with samples collected by Charles Darwin amongst many others. The UCT African studies special collections library wrote last night of the losses “ it houses some of the rare material from the 19th and 20th centuries: newspapers, periodicals, journals that contain information about the indigenous people and their(our) societies. Newspapers as Isigidimi samaXosa, Imvo Zabantsundu, Kafir express, Izwi, etc are all stored there. Early Xhosa and Zulu dictionaries, as well as unpublished collections of testimonies and folklore of Africans by African voices have this building as their storehouse. This is home to humanities researchers interested historical, language or sociological issues. Most of the early newspapers are digitized, but some issues are not.”

Over 3500 African films representing a 20 year collection have also been destroyed. People’s personal collections donated to Africa studies which had an impeccable reputation of archiving material. Some of the posts last night were from Patric Tariq Mellet who wrote “I am in tears. The African Studies Library at UCT is in flames. I lodged my printers archive of over 1500 publications that I printed over 14 years of exile when I ran the liberation movement printing press. These were mostly a record of the underground publications. It was a comprehensive record of my productions as a litho-printer... my contribution of printing day and night over all of those years.”

“ I'm thinking with absolute anguish of UCT Library Special Collections, including Ray Alexander Simons's papers, the Black Sash archives, some UDF collections ... my mind can't go further.” My own collection of footage documented in the 80’s may be amongst what has been destroyed.
People across the world are reeling from the full implications of what has been lost.

Press Release:


Things We Lost in the Fire

As Cape Town firefighters continue trying to control the fires around Table Mountain, the international academic community has responded with shock and sadness to the monumental damage to property and legacy that the University of Cape Town has suffered. Carte Blanche sifts through the ashes as experts in charge of the unique and priceless archives of personal papers and plant specimens dating back to the 1800s evaluate the impact of the fires. From rescuing irreplaceable struggle history documents to religious texts – we recount some of the week’s courageous acts.

Producer: Liz Fish | Researcher: Latashia Naidoo | Presenter: Derek Watts

Script:


Script: Sunday the 18th of April dawned a perfect windless day in Cape Town, cyclists, runners, and hikers were all out on the mountain. Lizette Lombard was running just above Rhodes Memorial
Lizette: I just first saw this little fume of smoke to the left hand side and Rhodes Memorial was to the right and I thought it was OK. And I was just going to continue with my trial run. And the next minute when I looked back at the fire, it was escalating at a tremendous speed.

TWITTER clip “ I think my car just got burnt at Rhodes memorial it spreading like wildfire”
Lizette: And there were two explosions that I later heard was the gas bottles of the Rhodes Memorial restaurant and I at that stage thought it was my car and then all of a sudden I had these fumes coming up right in front of me and then I really panicked and realised I had to run for my life

Script: A small fire started by a homeless person was reported at 9 am and fire crews were at the scene 45 minutes later. Then 4 helicopters were dispatched, but once it hit the historic stone pine trees below Rhodes Memorial, the fire accelerated rapidly spreading above and below the highway. Rhodes memorial restaurant went first, and then Mosterts Mill

Link: Built back in 1796 and remarkably this is the 1st time it has burnt in its 225 year history

Script: It was the oldest working mill in the country and part of the original Welgelegen farm. Laura Robinson says that tragically the restoration by the friends of Mostert’s Mill had just been completed
Derek: Looking at what remains, do you think it can be restored?
Laura:. ..they'll have to check for cracking and structural damage. But a lot of the timber work was part of the original restoration. And with the will and with the funds, it can be done yes, I think all of us would love to see it restored and operating again.
Script: Other historic buildings destroyed were the Millers house next door and Cadboll house down the road

Link” We have seen fires have raged across Table Mountain for decades and despite UCT being high up on the mountain, it’s never struck this century old campus. But this is where the greatest loss has been this week.”
Script: The world watched in horror as UCT was engulfed in smoke and images of students trying to save their residence went viral. The first thought was that the chemical engineering building would blow as its closest to the mountain, says VC Mamokgethi Phakeng
VC: when the fire erupted on the roof of the library, we were not even looking there. We were we were focused on areas that we thought those areas of risk of crisis, ….and boom, it came up on the roof of the jagger

Script: The images of all 3 floors of the 1930’s Jagger reading room on fire, were incomprehensible. It housed the internationally acclaimed African Studies collection, with its priceless and irreplaceable original manuscripts, paintings and photographs - the history of a nation. Executive director of libraries Ujala Satgoor, says the fire curtains had been tested just the week before, saving the rest of the libraries
Ujala: I think this is one of the worst nightmares of any library director in the world to be witness to such devastation and destruction of the human record What do you need to do to rebuild it?

Link “ The heart of any university is the library and every UCT graduate remembers Jagger with a sense of reverence, spending endless hours of their academic lives there.
Script: The 70 000-item African Studies Published Print Collection started in 1953 was destroyed, the entire 20 year African Studies Film Collection of 3 and a half thousand films, Government Publications from South Africa and across the continent. All critical teaching and research tools.

Link: People have invested their family archives, struggle history, films and photographs to UCT because their dusty damp garages weren’t the place for this invaluable history.

Script: For special collections and rare books librarian Tanya Simons- Barben, who spent 37 years of her life here, it’s unbearable

Tanya: So much loss part my soul. Part of myself, they were my babies I loved them more than my own family

Script: She is the daughter of Jack Simons, struggle icon and academic who spent 25 years in exile with her mother veteran trade unionist, Ray Alexander. Both were prolific writers and the Simons Collection formed a critical part of Apartheid history, alongside the Black Sash collection.

Tanya For decades, dedicated librarians and archivists have been collecting material, cataloguing, recording them, caring for them, conserving them hard, hard work. Lifetimes of professional work. African studies was a jewel in the crown and considered so by researchers from all over the world

Script: But it’s also her family archive of letters written by them in exile

Tanya” my experience of being banned, the birth of my two sons, all of that you know could possibly have gone

Link. “So many have a special treasure or artefact housed on campus and a young Rabbi braved the barricades to rescue the Holy Torah.
Rabbi: We went through about three or four blockades. Disaster risk management was there, um, and we just knew we had to we had to get there.

Script: Rabbi Nissen Goldman was relieved to find the Kaplan Centre for Jewish studies wasn't on fire but running into thick smoke, he saved the Rachel Bloch Torah brought from Israel in 1950

Rabbi” I got a call this morning from the, uh, son of Rachel Bloch, whose Torah this belongs to saying when he saw the picture he just started crying

Script: But other parts of campus were ablaze, like the roof of the HW Pearson building. It had been a horrendous 24 hours for Tony Verboom, head of Biological Sciences who gained access for the first time that morning

Upsound Tony “this turret sits directly above the bolus herbarium which houses a globally important collection of plant specimens and obviously having a hole in the roof above the herbarium is a problem

Script: Thankfully the 350 000 specimen collection, dating back to 1835, was intact, but they are preserved on paper, and water was seeping out from under the cabinets.

Derek “What is the Bolus Herbarium all about

Tony: OK, so Herbarium is basically a collection of dried plant speciemens. It's like a dictionary but when it comes to names of plants organisms we need a specimens to attach that name to

Derek basically this herbarium represents centuries of work.

Tony: Yeah. And if you lose this herbarium, our entire nomenclature system is unhinged which is a serious problem.

Script: But the iCWild unit and the plant conservation unit were destroyed, which housed the original slide collection and lifetime work of Professor Tim Hoffman. The good news was the pollen collection survived.

But academics and students are in a state of shock. The early evacuation of the 3 and a half thousand students and their valiant efforts to extinguish the fire, saved their lives. But everyone is in limbo, academics are having to rethink their entire programmes

VC: Some of them were in the middle of their work. All of that stops. Some of them might have to rethink what they do for their masters or their PHd. They might have to look for other access to material elsewhere in the world

Script Now it’s a race against time, they started draining the water from the basement just below the reading room floor, on Tuesday.

Ujala: We may be losing originals, but in some cases we would have access to digitized content. I know there's a huge concern about the San and Khoi collections, etc. We can say that to you know, some of those collections are intact

Script: There has been a global outpouring of support both in terms of restoration and finances but most critically, to recover as much material as possible
Ujala: Based on previous disasters, if you look at the destruction of the National Library of Sri Lanka, Egypt, etc, Timbuktu, a group of librarians have started an online community and putting out a call to researchers and academics who've used us and say, can you then upload the materials that you used
Script: But priceless collections are feared lost, like the original copy of a bible dating back to 1535
Tanya: It's not only the struggle material, it's the whole caboodle. The development of the human mind
Script: It’s been a week of shock, grief, and finger pointing,- enormous losses and near misses. A cataclysmic event in the intellectual history of the University, and of the country. But the solidarity with the University, the firemen, and the students has been remarkable.
VC: It's a great tragedy, but with each tragedy comes an opportunity. We are determined to bounce back stronger from this.
